S35.01.needs: a Managed Cloud account on a plan granted Deep Research, and a research-capable model
S35.01.note: The Deep research toggle shows only in Cloud mode, with a research-capable model and the canUseDeepResearch grant.
steps: Sign in to a Managed Cloud account and open a chat.
Check the model picker shows a model that supports research; the toggle is hidden for other models.
Tap Add to chat beside the message box.
Turn on Deep research.
Type a research question and send it.
Look for a Deep research card in the reply that shows a phase such as Planning research. Compare with Expected.
S35.01.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (button beside the message box) > Deep research

labels.text: Review the plan to start searching

S35.04.needs: a Managed Cloud account with Deep Research and a run that stops at plan approval
S35.04.note: The editor helper text reads Edit any step before it runs. Only these steps are searched.
steps: Start a Deep research run (S35.01).
Wait until the card shows Review the plan to start searching.
Edit the text of Step 1 (placeholder Describe what to search), tap Remove step on a step, and tap Add a step.
Tap Approve plan.
Look that only the edited steps are searched and the card moves on. Compare with Expected.
S35.04.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > plan editor (phase Review the plan to start searching)

S35.09.needs: a Managed Cloud account with Deep Research and a run that is still going
S35.09.note: The counts line and elapsed time are hidden until there is a count or time above zero.
steps: Start a run and approve the plan (S35.01, S35.04).
Watch the phase text under the card, for example Searching the web.
Read the counts line under the title (round, searches, sources) once a search has run.
Read the elapsed time at the top right of the card and check it keeps going.
Compare with Expected.
S35.09.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply, while the run is going

S35.10.needs: a Managed Cloud account with Deep Research
S35.10.note: Research plan is an accessibility label, not printed text. Status words (Queued, In progress, Done, Failed, Not run) are only spoken, not printed.
steps: Start a run and approve the plan (S35.01, S35.04).
Look at the list of plan steps under the card once the editor is closed.
Check each step shows its text and an icon, and the step being searched changes as the run goes.
Compare with Expected.
S35.10.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > Research plan list (after plan approval)

S35.11.needs: a finished Deep Research run that used web sources
S35.11.note: The heading text is a template; the number is the count of sources.
steps: Finish a Deep research run that used web sources.
Scroll below the reply to the sources block.
Read the heading with the count, then the numbered source chips with title and URL.
If there are more sources than the chip limit, use the expand control.
Compare the list with Expected.
S35.11.where: Chat screen > Deep research card or reply > Sources list

S35.12.needs: a Managed Cloud account with at least one finished report
S35.12.note: Source chips take a snippet, but the code does not confirm the excerpt shows on screen; no separate collection view was found.
steps: Open Reports from the sidebar (S35.25).
Open a finished report.
Scroll to the end of the report.
Read the Sources list and tap a source chip, then Open page to see its web page.
Compare with Expected.
S35.12.where: Reports > open a finished report > Sources list at the end of the report

S35.13.needs: a finished report with key findings and plan questions
S35.13.note: Searched research files for findings and question grouping. The report shows one flat Key findings list (ReportsScreen.tsx) and Sections grouped by report headings (ResearchReportSections.tsx); no view grouping findings under each question was found.

labels.text: Paused. Resume to continue from where it stopped.

S35.17.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a research run that is still running
S35.17.note: Pause is not offered during Writing report. A failed pause shows Could not pause this research. It is still running. (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx)
steps: Start a run and wait until it shows Searching the web (S35.01, S35.04).
Tap Pause; the button changes to Pausing.
Look for Research paused and the text Paused. Resume to continue from where it stopped.
Tap Resume.
Check the phase returns to searching and the counts continue from where they stopped. Compare with Expected.
S35.17.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > Pause, then Resume

S35.18.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a running research task
S35.18.note: No visible text for a cancelled plan was found in non-test code; the words Research plan cancelled appear only in a test file. Server-side recording (research-loop.ts) was not checked.
steps: Start a run and wait until it is searching (S35.01, S35.04).
Tap Stop.
Look for the phase Research stopped and the text Stopped before it finished.
To test Cancel instead, start a run and tap Cancel at the plan step, then check the card.
Compare with Expected, which also asks that the stop is recorded as a cancel.
S35.18.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in the reply > Stop (during a run) or Cancel (at plan approval)

S35.19.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a run that was stopped or failed
S35.19.note: The report list shows the raw status word, and the reader does not print the word partial. The chat shows Sources so far for partial sources. Whether a partial report is produced depends on the server, not checked.
steps: Stop a run (S35.18), or use one that failed.
Open Reports from the sidebar.
Find that run in the list and check its row for a small badge with a warning icon and a status word.
Open it and read the error box if one is shown.
Compare with Expected, which asks that a partial report is labelled as partial.
S35.19.where: Reports > open a report from a run that was stopped or failed

S35.20.needs: a Managed Cloud account with at least one finished report
S35.20.note: The sidebar route to the drawer group was read from DrawerContent.tsx, not run on a device.
steps: Open the sidebar and tap Reports (it is in the folded group of the sidebar).
Tap a report row.
Check the title at the top of the reader, the summary, the Key findings list, the Sections box and the body text.
Scroll to the bottom and check the Sources list.
Compare with Expected.
S35.20.where: Sidebar > Reports > tap a report row

S35.21.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a report that has three or more headings
S35.21.note: The outline in the reader shows only at three or more headings.
steps: Open Reports and open a report with three or more headings.
Find the Sections box above the report body.
Tap a section name to jump to its heading.
Check the reader scrolls to that section. Compare with Expected.
In a chat reply, tap Show report sections to expand the outline.
S35.21.where: Reports > open a report > Sections box (shown when the report has three or more headings)

S35.22.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a report that has citations
S35.22.note: Tapping a number inside the body text was not confirmed in the code; the source chips are the confirmed path.
steps: Open a report that has sources.
Tap a source chip in the Sources list at the end of the report.
Look for the action sheet with Open page and tap it.
Check the source web page opens. Compare with Expected.
S35.22.where: Reports > open a report > tap a source chip under Sources, then Open page

S35.23.needs: a report that contains a table or a chart; the code does not say which reports do
S35.23.note: Charts are drawn from mermaid fenced blocks (ReportChart); no visible title for a chart was found.
steps: Open a report whose body has a table.
Scroll the table sideways if it is wider than the screen.
Look for a chart drawn in the body of a report that has a chart block.
Compare with Expected.
S35.23.where: Reports > open a report (tables and charts appear in the body)

S35.25.needs: a Managed Cloud account; an empty list or one with past reports
S35.25.note: The empty-state text says Turn on Research in the composer, but the toggle is labelled Deep research (AddToChatSheet.tsx).
steps: Open the sidebar and tap Reports.
If the list is empty, check for No reports yet and the line about turning on Research.
If there are reports, check each row shows a date, a source count and a model name.
Tap a row to reopen it, then go back.
Scroll to the bottom to load older reports. Compare with Expected.

S35.26.needs: a Managed Cloud account with a finished research run
S35.26.note: Pull to refresh on the Reports list only reloads the list; it does not rerun research.
steps: Open a chat with a finished Deep research run (card shows Research complete).
Tap Run again.
Look for the card to start again with a new phase such as Planning research or Searching the web.
Compare the new results with the old ones. Compare with Expected.
S35.26.where: Chat screen > Deep research card in a finished run > Run again

S35.33.needs: a phone with notifications allowed for the app and a Deep Research run
S35.33.note: The row shows only when the research feature flag is on and the server announces the group. The settings text mentions only ready reports, not failures; push taps open Reports (productLinks.ts).
steps: Open Settings and tap Notifications.
Find the Research complete row; its description reads When a research report is ready.
Turn it on, then start a Deep research run and leave the app.
Wait for the run to finish and check for a push notification or an in-app notice.
Compare with Expected, which also covers a failed run.
